questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068270/assets/7cb71517fe60c9d15b6cacddbf5f91c2e4a60103b8917a4d9baa287517a5fd54.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(-3,-1),$ and passes through the point $(-5,1).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-3,-1),$ and so we have

$$
x+3=p{t}^{2},\,y+1=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(-5,1),$ we can substitute $x=-5$ and $y=1$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2=p{t}^{2} \\ 2=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ 1 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ -2 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ -2 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+3=(-\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},\,y+1=2(-\frac{1}{2})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+3=-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y+1=-t.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x+3=2t,\,y-2={t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x+3}{2},\,{t}^{2}=y-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=y-2$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{4} & =y-2 \\ (x+3)^{2} & =4(y-2).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x+1=-\frac{5}{4}{t}^{2},\,y-1=-\frac{5}{2}t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-\frac{4(x+1)}{5},\,t=-\frac{2(y-1)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{2(y-1)}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4(y-1)^{2}}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{4(x+1)}{5}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4(y-1)^{2}}{25} & =-\frac{4(x+1)}{5} \\ (y-1)^{2} & =\frac{25}{4}\cdot (-\frac{4(x+1)}{5}) \\ (y-1)^{2} & =-5(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(4,4),$ and passes through the point $(8,8).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(4,4),$ and so we have

$$
x-4=p{t}^{2},\,y-4=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(8,8),$ we can substitute $x=8$ and $y=8$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}4=p{t}^{2} \\ 4=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 4 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 4 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =\frac{4}{4} \\ p & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-4=(1){t}^{2},\,y-4=2(1)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-4={t}^{2},\,y-4=2t.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following parametric equation of the parabola

$$
x+7=-3t,\,y-2=-9{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of this parabola is

$(x\,+$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =-\frac{x+7}{3},\,{t}^{2}=-\frac{1}{9}(y-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{x+7}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x+7)^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{1}{9}(y-2)$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+7)^{2}}{9} & =-\frac{1}{9}(y-2) \\ {(x+7)}^{2} & =-(y-2)\end{aligned}
$$
